newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat 1996 operating profits fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: Fiat 1996 operating profits fall sharply.

text.p: Italy's industrial giant Fiat on Thursday said its 1996 operating profit fell sharply to around 1.8 trillion lire after 1995's 3.325 trillion lire, while sales rose three percent to around 78 trillion lire.

In the group's traditional letter to shareholders, Fiat reported that 1996 pretax profit would rise slightly to around 3.5 trillion lire from 1995's 3.404 trillion lire, while its operating margin across the whole group slipped to 2.3 percent from 4.4 percent in 1995.
The group added that its operating margin for its industrial sales fell to 2.8 percent from 1995's 4.8 percent.

Fiat said its 1996 pretax profits were boosted by the partial flotation of its agricultural and construction machinery division New Holland and the capital gain from the sale of its Prime fund management arm to Italian insurer Generali.
The company said its net debt fell to two trillion lire at the end of 1996 from 2.597 trillion lire at end-1995.
Fiat painted a generally cautious picture for 1997, pointing out that economic conditions were difficult in Italy and in many other nations.
